result:
I changed `_get_client_hello` in `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py` so QUIC flows no longer stall when `allow_hosts` or `ignore_hosts` is set. I haven't run the tests, and I didn't add one.

In the UDP branch, the parsers now run only when the data looks like that protocol, which is what the TCP branch already does. The QUIC parser is tried only if `_starts_like_quic(data_client, context.server.address)` is true. The DTLS parser is tried only if `starts_like_dtls_record(data_client)` is true.

With the empty `b""` that arrives after the QUIC TLS handshake, neither check passes. `_get_client_hello` returns `None` instead of the `ValueError` becoming `NeedsMoreData`. `_next_layer` then continues past the ignore check and assigns an `HttpLayer`.

A test would go in `test/mitmproxy/addons/test_next_layer.py`: a UDP context with `ignore_hosts` set, calling `_next_layer` with `b""` and expecting a layer rather than `NeedsMoreData`.
